cases.name: Mary Elizabeth Horton Vail
cases.about: She was the 1957 homecoming queen and editor of the school newspaper at Eunice High School in Louisiana. She attended McNeese State College and was a 2nd grade teacher at Moss Bluff Elementary School.
cases.narrative:
On 10/30/1962, her body was pulled from the Calcasieu River in Lake Charles, LA. He claimed she drowned while they were out fishing but he had taken out life insurance on her two months earlier and an autopsy later revealed she had a large 4-inch bruise to the back of her head and neck and a scarf pushed 4 inches into her mouth.

A pathologist who examined her autopsy report believes Mary was forcibly asphyxiated and possibly struck with an oar before her body went in the river.

cases.name: Danielle Nichole Walker
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "She was the youngest of four siblings and was definitely the fiery one out of them all. Danielle was known to always say what was on her mind no matter the place, time and to who it was. She will be remembered as the light in her family and friend's life.

Danielle was known to laugh anywhere she went and it would always become infectious. If you knew her, you'd know that sitting next to Danielle would get you trouble for laughing and you could count on it happening every time.

After graduating from Alfred M. Barbe High School in 2006, Danielle attended SOWELA Technical College for nursing and graduated in the Fall of 2022 as an LPN. She absolutely loved her profession and aspired to grow which gave her a goal to become an RN one day.

Danielle had a strong personal relationship with God and became a member of Christian Baptist Church. Her attendance and fellowship here enabled her to grow her faith as she navigated life with her precious children whom she adored with every bit of her love. Danielle was always willing to do for her sons, even if it meant her going without to give to them."
